editors-message.title: Clear Skies ahead
editors-message.byline: Caitlin Bernal and Gabriel Renee Quizan
editors-message.article:
SOARING ABOVE lofty expectations, the Ateneo Blue Eagles showcased a series of outstanding and historic performances in the first semester of the University Athletic Association of the Philippines’ (UAAP) Season 88. Across a nine-sport schedule, the Blue and White brought home eight podium finishes and three championships—a testament to the exemplary caliber embodied forth by the University’s student-athletes.

With the UAAP gearing up for a packed second-semester slate, the Blue Eagles look to end Season 88 on a high note as they carry the Ateneo banner with beaming pride and fiery resolve.

The second installment of Season 88 will follow 20 teams on 20 different journeys, all united by a single goal of reaching the UAAP pinnacle. This semester’s primer aims to reemphasize the collective drive and passion embodied by the Blue Eagles.

As the dedication to attaining greatness intensifies in Loyola Heights, The GUIDON Sports remains an attentive chronicler of the unique Atenean sportsperson journey. From the Blue Eagles’ pursuit of knowledge in the classroom to their zeal for athletic mastery, the publication stays committed to being the voice of Blue Eagle excellence.

As our student-athletes strive to scale daring heights, let us, the Ateneo community, rally with them in every fight, fall, and victory.

mens-basketball.title: Rising Above
mens-basketball.article:
FOLLOWING A tough UAAP Season 87 showing, the Ateneo Men’s 3x3 Basketball Team looks to turn the page after their one-win campaign.

With second-year Head Coach and former Ateneo standout Nico Salva, the Blue Eagles continue their mission of building a more competitive program for the upcoming season. This mission was reflected in last season’s squad, composed of Andre Tan, Danger Tupas, Adam Dela Cruz, and Sam Reyes.

For Season 88, Ateneo aims to showcase the lessons that they have learned and embrace the growth from last season’s challenges. Repping the court this time around will be Team A mainstays Shawn Tuano, Drew Bongo, Kyle Gamber, and Thirdy Ebdane.

As 3x3 basketball continues to rise in popularity, the Katipunan-based unit remains determined to reclaim their place at the top of the sport in the UAAP arena. With a renewed focus and sense of teamwork, the Blue Eagles are ready to soar and get buckets this Season 88.

Editor’s Note: The publication has chosen to feature Head Coach Nico Salva in lieu of a team captain, with the finalization of the Men’s 3x3 Basketball roster still in progress prior to the completion of the primer.

womens-basketball.title: The gold standard
womens-basketball.article:
SHOCKING THE UAAP basketball scene with their Cinderella first-place finish in Season 87, the Ateneo Women’s 3x3 Basketball Team sets their sight on a repeat title in Season 88 to prove that their breakthrough was no fluke.

After capturing their first-ever gold medal finish in last year’s competition, Head Coach PJ Navarro, alongside confirmed returnees Kai Oani and Lauren Lopez, are back in tow in pursuit of a back-to-back championship.

The Blue and White enters the season eager to deliver another impressive showing under Head Coach Navarro. As defending champions, the Blue Eagles embrace both the challenge of heightened expectations and the pressures that come with it.

Following their narrow exit in the semifinals on the 5-on-5 stage, Ateneo’s perennial 3x3 squad is intent on reasserting their place among the UAAP’s elite.

That focus now shifts to the 3x3 circuit, where belief forged in gold and resolve strengthened by adversity fuel the Katipunan-based squad’s bid to remain the gold standard of the Women’s division.

Editor’s Note: The publication has chosen to feature Head Coach PJ Navarro in lieu of a team captain, with the finalization of the Women’s 3x3 Basketball roster still in progress prior to the completion of the primer.

mens-blitz-chess.title: Setting the tempo
mens-blitz-chess.article:
With the introduction of the Blitz and Rapid Chess Tournaments in Season 87, the Ateneo Men’s Chess Team (AMCT) capped their maiden Blitz campaign in last place after struggling to find dominant form on the boards.

Despite their struggles, the Blue and White successfully secured individual honors for their exploits, headlined by silver medalist Manuel Maglunog and bronze medalist Knarf Batislaong.

Running it back with the same flock of Blue Eagles from last semester’s Classical Tournament, Classical medalists Team Captain Khalil Kis-ing and promising rookie Ritchie James Abeleda aim to translate their first semester success in the faster-paced format. As veterans like Batislaong and Maglunog return to the board, the team not only has an obvious pedigree, but also the chances of team glory.

With a mixture of returning individual prowess and newfound team chemistry, Ateneo sets out to go as far as possible in their journey up the chess pedestal.

womens-blitz-chess.title: Built to blitz
womens-blitz-chess.article:
LIKE LIGHTNING—the Ateneo Women’s Blitz Chess Team returns to the UAAP with an instant attack.

Coming off a stunning championship clinch, the Blue Eagles are eager to keep steady, finding strength in their tempo. Crowned and cunning, this Jan Garcia-coached unit intends to carry a mindset of focus, grit, and learning as they look to dominate the boards.

This season, the Blue and White is coming in with its cast of seasoned gunners.. Among the returning seniors are Kristine Flores, Jiessel Marino, and Glesit Tatoy, together with juniors Alphecca Gonzales and Team Captain Elayza Villa. With a legacy to leave, these veterans are dedicated to solidifying a lasting lineage by priming emerging rookies, including Francine Magpily to take the mantle.

For the team, this sport became a two-way learning process that reminds them to always keep their feet on the ground. According to the team, they are transformed by the game as much as they change it in every move they make. With much space to flourish, the regal Women’s Blitz Chess powerhouse awaits their turn to make their tactical strike.

mens-beach-volleyball.title: Dynamic Resurgence
mens-beach-volleyball.article:
MISSING THE podium since Season 86, the Ateneo Men’s Beach Volleyball Team (AMBVT) seeks to reinstate glory in the outdoor scene with iron-clad chemistry.

While the AMBVT struggled to amass victories last season, nabbing only one win against the University of the East, the sun shines again on the Blue and White as former Rookie of the Year Jian Salarzon returns to the sands.

Having clinched bronze in Season 85, the dynamic duo of Team Captains Amil Pacinio and Salarzon aim to spearhead the Blue Eagles’ success and revive their diagonal brilliance. With experience in both indoor and outdoor volleyball, their capabilities shall aid the AMBVT’s campaign towards attaining a podium finish.

Veterans Miguel Yu, Karl Corrigedor, and Anjo Almadro also bring sheer will and talent to the composition, with familiarity being the Blue Eagles’ foremost strength towards greatness. Mentoring them is Coach Henry James Pecaña, who has guided the AMBVT since 2022.

In his final year as a Blue Eagle, Pacinio hopes to secure a final four resurgence for the Ateneo and reclaim the AMBVT’s excellence on the sands.

womens-beach-volleyball.title: Purpose in Play
womens-beach-volleyball.article:
HONOR AND dedication—bearing the Blue and White banner is what keeps the Ateneo Women’s Beach Volleyball Team driven and able to power through past obstacles.

Last Season 87, the Blue Eagles struggled to find their footing in the sands, landing at a sixth-place finish. Despite this adversity, Katipunan’s unyielding beach volleyball tandems remain crowned in courage as they head into a new season. Hungry to rebound with resilience, Ateneo introduces a reinforced system—one that is primed for a Final Four return after six years.

At the core of this new system are battle-tested frontrunners Grydelle Matibag, Liz Lomocso, and Christen Quimpo. Conditioned to embody discipline each day, they are now set to return under the heat, hell-bent on steering their stint towards a well-earned comeback. The lineup draws strength from one another, highlighting the importance of communication and support. Still shaped by the expertise of Head Coach Henry James Pecaña, the roster aims to return to the league with pride for their team, for the school, and for the people who believe in their revival.

mens-swimming.title: Bloodline of Brilliance
mens-swimming.article:
FAST AND fearless—the Ateneo Men’s Swimming Team has long been the kings of the UAAP waters.

The Blue Eagles are no stranger to domination, as their nine years of command demonstrate an unwavering drive to prolong their reign. With a double-digit dynasty in sight, this lineup under Coach Archie Lim is committed to adding another jewel to their crown.

With veterans Rian Tirol, Rafael Barreto, and Charles Ticbaen returning for the last time, the perennial titleholders intend to maintain a tightly run fleet. Alongside them are rookies National Collegiate Athletic Association Season 100 Juniors Championship team members TJ Amaro and Rune Tan, as well as Palarong Pambansa multi-medalists Paolo Labanan and Juan Suarez. As they debut in college, the inheritors of the Ateneo banner will carry the team’s spirit, ensuring the squad’s continued dominance. Rounding out the star-studded line-up is Season 87 Rookie of the Year and Most Valuable Player Miguel Barreto, who is hungry to return to the competition and collect more hardware for Loyola Heights.

Even as undisputed leaders of the collegiate sport, Team Captains Ticbaen and Joshua Del Rio refuse to get comfortable, sustaining the same hunger and hustle from the very start. With a gold-medal glory in their veins, the unshakeable Ateneo swimming empire is on track for a ten-year uninterrupted surge.

womens-swimming.title: Champions of the Current
womens-swimming.article:
SEEKING TO forge their championship glory into a dynasty, the Ateneo Women’s Swimming Team is determined to relive their dominant run in UAAP Season 88.

After clinching their first gold finish since Season 82, the Blue Eagles set their sights on securing back-to-back titles in this year’s ultimate race. Joining the flock are standout rookies—former Palarong Pambansa prodigy Mia Barretto, regional gold medalist Rissa Sahagun, and returning Season 87 Most Valuable Player Mishka Sy, among others. Bolstered by the promising selection of swimmers, Ateneo mainstay Team Captain Kirsten Manuel asserts that the Blue and White are geared up for another golden finish.

Manuel and the team welcome rising expectations as challenges, so long as they remain grounded in their winning synergy. “As long as we stay committed and work together as a team, we like where we’re headed,” says the veteran swimmer.

Anchoring poise under pressure, the Blue Eagles look to intensify the waves of Season 88 with a myriad of podium finishes and a titanic medal haul.

mens-badminton.title: Drive to the Top
mens-badminton.article:
GROUNDED IN grit, the Ateneo Men’s Badminton Team (AMBT) enters UAAP Season 88 with one mission: to reclaim the crown.

After bowing to the National University Bulldogs in the finals last season, the Blue Eagles are banking on a battle-tested veteran core and a wave of fresh talent to mount another serious title bid.

Stepping into the role of Team Captain is seasoned stalwart Lyrden Laborte. He is set to reprise the role he shared last season with Arthur ‘Pingkoy’ Salvado, who will be entering his final year of eligibility. Joining Laborte as Co-Captain is fellow veteran Lance Vargas, who is eager to make a statement in his third year of competition.

In addition, the Blue Eagles welcome NCAA Season 100 Juniors Division MVP Zeth Quiambao and 2024 Palarong Pambansa gold medalist Jamal Rahmat Pandi—two young guns looking to make their mark in the collegiate scene.

Led by acclaimed Head Coach Kennie Asuncion-Robles, the Blue and White are primed to be a formidable force. With rackets in hand, the Katipunan-based squad now sets its sights on smashing through the competition once again.

womens-badminton.title: Reclaiming the Throne
womens-badminton.article:
LOOKING TO restore their place on top, the Ateneo Women’s Badminton Team (AWBT) is determined to reclaim the UAAP crown after their seven year reign ended in Season 87.

Leading the charge in their quest for greatness are Team Captains Mika De Guzman and Jochelle Alvarez. Making her highly anticipated return this season, Alvarez will provide much-needed experience alongside De Guzman, as the former Co-Most Valuable Players aim to fuel their squad with an unwavering determination and a shared hunger for Blue and White excellence.

Reinforcing the roster is reigning Rookie of the Year, Althea Ocampo, who looks to amplify the roster’s firepower and further elevate her game. Together with new recruits Daena Louise Castro and Althea Princess Hernandez, the Blue Eagles are more than ready for the challenges that lie ahead next season.

With a more seasoned roster bolstering a mix of youth and experience, the AWBT have their eyes set on redemption as they storm the court with a renewed drive to reclaim their spot at the top.

mens-track-and-field.title: Pushing Past Limits
mens-track-and-field.article:
AFTER A promising two-gold medal haul last year, the Ateneo Men’s Track and Field Team (AMTF) is determined to solidify its status as bona fide contenders this UAAP Season 88. Fueled by their nascent squad’s emerging brilliance, the Blue Eagles are dead set on disrupting the league status quo.

Captaining Ateneo’s pursuit for excellence this season is reigning UAAP and Philippine discus throw record holder Russel Ricaforte. Alongside him are 800-meter gold medalist Hassan Loraña and veteran thrower Emilio Perez, who aim to carry last year’s momentum for more podium finishes in the oval. Meanwhile, touted rookies like middle-distance runner Hussein Loraña and sprinter Matthew Luis Angeles seek to make their mark in the collegiate scene and inject firepower into the Blue Eagles’ budding unit.

Under the guidance of Head Coach Sean Guevara, the Katipunan-based squad is primed to ascend into the UAAP’s zenith. With their eyes fixed on glory, the AMTF gears up to challenge for the crown and redefine the odds this season.

womens-track-and-field.title: Full Throttle
womens-track-and-field.article:
YOUNG AND fearless, the Ateneo Women’s Track and Field Team aims to be a force to be reckoned with this UAAP Season 88. Led by Head Coach Sean Guevara, the eight-eagle lineup is poised to take on the juggernauts of the league with grit, determination, and undying perseverance.

Veterans Krisha Aguillon and Kat Duavit look to spread their wings for the Blue and White with renewed experience. In addition, rookies Rhea Lego, Jonalyn Halasan, and Shanenn Guevarra charge onto the track as versatile neophytes, and thrower Yden Candelario brings power to the field. Together, they round out a squad hungry for a race nothing short of electric.

With Team Captain Francesca Cheng setting the tone alongside fellow sprint specialist Sammie Souza, the Blue Eagles are racing toward personal bests, stronger bonds, and a season full of bold, unrelenting strides.

mens-table-tennis.title: Destiny Inbound
mens-table-tennis.article:
THE ATENEO Men’s Table Tennis Team (AMTTT) aims to take down the Growling Tigers’ dynasty and capture the gold after a steady second-place finish last Season 87.

As Season 88 begins with unsettled business, returning Team Captain Andrew Uy and newly-appointed Co-captain Mahendra Cabrido lead a contending team with the hefty task of finishing their story destined for gold. Bolstered by veterans Wrency Abad, Zherdel Fresco, and Andree Garcia, the AMTTT is loaded with talent ripe for a championship run.

Additionally, the AMTTT is backed by incoming rookies Carlos Docto, a Palarong Pambansa bronze medalist in mixed doubles, and Emmanuel Yamson, who look to add youth to this experienced squad.

With accomplished Head Coach Mihali Crisostomo at the helm, the team finds themselves brimming with experience and flair coming into the next season.

Possessing three straight silver finishes over the years, the AMTTT has the chance to perfect their masterpiece, topping their journey off with a storybook championship.

womens-table-tennis.title: Rally to Glory
womens-table-tennis.article:
SOARING TO new heights following a second-place finish in Season 86 and a bronze medal in Season 87, the Ateneo Women’s Table Tennis Team (AWTTT) aims to capture the ever-elusive gold in Season 88. The Blue Eagles enter the season hungry as ever, blending experience with youth on their way to the top.

Keen on turning individual weaknesses into collective strengths, returning Team Captain Celeen Docto, along with Co-captain and Season 86 Rookie of the Year Jelaine Monteclaro, look to spearhead the Blue Eagles atop the podium. With returning veteran Pia Fabregar back in tow, the Blue Eagles add another veteran to their already stacked core, including Gredel De Guzman and Aubrey Solis.

Bolstering the team’s campaign are Palarong Pambansa Secondary Girls Doubles Gold medalist Andrea Deondo, along with fellow rookies Nicole Alemania and Trisha Pachica. All eager to join in the team’s culture built on trust, resilience, and shared determination for growth, the sought-after recruits look to make an impact in Season 88.

With the new season on the horizon, the Blue Eagles are looking primed and ready to rise above previous challenges and finally reach the pinnacle of UAAP glory.

cheerdance.title: Progress over Perfection
cheerdance.article:
AFTER CONCLUDING the previous season’s UAAP Cheerdance Competition at eighth place, the Blue Babble Battalion is ravenous to rise and prevail in their next major showcase. Spearheaded by Team Captains Victor Medina, Gabrielle Santiago, and Geryna Abarcar, Ateneo remains dedicated to building progress with stronger foundations and louder chants for the upcoming Season 88.

The Blue Eagles return with sharpened wings—recalibrating routines and resetting mindsets as a wide set of fresh talents enter the promising roster. At Head Coach JP Santiago’s helm, Gabby Calilung, Maxine Vela, and Luis Arroyo lead their fellow rookies in cementing fresh discipline with fierce passion into their groundwork.

More than just being the underdogs, the Katipunan-based squad aims to introduce their young unit as a family that stewards and shepherds each other. Strengthening synergy is Ateneo’s top priority, as they look forward to orchestrating a stellar performance on the UAAP dancefloor.
